newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Santander seeks growth in Brazil retail banking.
newsitem.headline: Santander seeks growth in Brazil retail banking.

text.p: Spanish banking group Banco Santander SA said it aims to expand considerably its business in Brazil as economic stability has opened an enormous opportunity for growth in retail banking.
Santander, which last March acquired a controlling stake in local bank Banco Geral do Comercio, plans to broaden the bank's branch network to 200 branches from the current 42 in the next three years.
It hopes its client base will grow to between 300,000 and 400,000 from 80,000 today.
"We are convinced that Brazil's market potential is huge," Antonio Horta Osorio, president of Santander Group in Brazil, told a news conference Thursday.

Osorio said the amount of banking loans to the private sector in Brazil accounts for 30 percent of gross domestic product, well below the U.S. and other Latin American countries such as Chile and Colombia. In the U.S., banking loans represent 130 percent of GDP.
He also pointed out that the number of checking accounts in the country is still extremely low compared with Japan, for instance, where there are three accounts for each person.
Osorio said Santander wants to grow in southern and southeastern Brazil, where 85 percent of the country's total deposits are concentrated.
The bank, however, has not yet decided whether it will expand its network by buying other banks or building its own branches.
"We are studying several ways to expand," Osorio said, sidestepping questions about market rumors that Santander was about to conclude a deal to acquire local bank Banco Noroeste.
He also said the group is willing to study privatization opportunities in the banking sector like Banco Meridional and

Osorio also said the Brazilian operations will complement Santander's businesses in other Latin American countries. Currently, the group owns nine commercial banks and seven investment banks in the region.
The bank wants to target the millions of Brazilians who are now joining the consumer world due to the success of the government's anti-inflation efforts.
"In the last three years, about 10 million Brazilians gained access to the consumer market. We expect that, in the next four or five years, another 10 million will also be joining it," Osorio said.
Santander will provide services to clients with a minimum monthly income of 1,000 reais and offer all kinds of products, including credit card, consumer credit, real estate credit and car financing.
Osorio said he expects all branches still under the Banco Geral do Comercio brand name to carry the Banco Santander Brasil SA name within three months.
Santander is Spain's largest financial conglomerate, with a net worth of $5.0 billion, $150 billion in total assets, 70,000 employees and 11 million clients.

It is also the biggest international financial group in Latin America. Investment in the region has totalled $3.4 billion in the last few years and the bank expects to show a profit of $400 million in Latin America in 1997.
